findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the concrete declaration syntax for the provenance fields (e.g. an indented sub-list of `environment:`/`principal:`/`privilege_posture:` lines directly under the owning `[operator-attested]` AC checkbox item) and state the rule that binds a declaration to its AC item, so both the DET presence check and the AGENT probe parse and associate the same shape.
evidence: Plan: 'a det_-style check mirroring src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py ... It asserts the fields EXIST and are non-placeholder'

det_operator_attested.ac_item_lines returns only single `- [ ]` checkbox lines and _OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE matches a single inline tag on one line — the module has no notion of a multi-line, multi-field declaration attached to an AC item
The three fields include 'a one-line justification' — a structured, multi-field payload that cannot sit on one checkbox line the way the [operator-attested] tag does
The rubric decision rule (a) 'declared environment vs the in-repo IaC anchor' presumes a locatable `environment` value, but no declaration syntax is defined for the AGENT criterion to read either
findings.finding: The plan does not specify the textual form or location of the three provenance fields (environment / principal / privilege_posture + one-line justification) within the ticket, yet both the deterministic presence check and the AGENT contradiction probe depend on locating them — and, for the DET check, associating them with their owning [operator-attested] AC item.
scenarios: The DET check cannot decide WHERE to look for the fields (sub-bullet under the AC item? a key:value block? a fenced YAML region? a separate ## Provenance section?), so its presence/non-placeholder assertion is unimplementable as specified
Two [operator-attested] AC items in one ticket: with no binding rule, the DET check cannot tell which declaration belongs to which criterion, so it cannot flag the one that is missing fields
The AGENT probe has no defined field to extract the declared account from before comparing it to versions.tf
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that the three fields are authored as an indented sub-block immediately following the `[operator-attested]` checkbox line (the AC item they belong to), give the exact key spelling, and have det_measurement_provenance parse that sub-block per AC item — extending det_operator_attested's ac_item_lines to also capture each item's continuation/sub-bullet lines rather than only the checkbox line.

evidence: 4 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

verify command `grep -rn 'project.measurement-provenance' src/rebar/` inspects output with `grep` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable

verify command `grep -rnE 'boto3|botocore|subprocess|requests|urllib|socket|httpx' src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py` inspects output with `grep` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly that the new rubric prompt's front-matter declares an agentic execution mode (not the sibling project prompts' single_turn), so its tool-using posture is authored intentionally rather than inherited from tool-less templates.
evidence: The AGENT-tier code-grounded reviewers plan_review_E4/T1/T10/T5c/G6.md all declare `execution_mode: agentic`
Plan (Scope, criteria_routing.json entry): 'At 1-TURN it would have no filesystem tooling and the contradiction probe could not run.'
findings.finding: The plan tells the author to model the new rubric prompt on the three existing .rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-*.md files, but all three declare `execution_mode: single_turn` — the tool-less mode — whereas the criterion's whole job requires reading infra/terraform/versions.tf, and every AGENT-tier code-reading criterion (E4/T1/T10/T5c/G6) carries `execution_mode: agentic`.
findings.location: Scope: '.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md ... follows the shape of the three existing .rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-*.md files'
scenarios: An implementer copies a sibling project prompt verbatim (as instructed) and inherits `execution_mode: single_turn`; the routing exec:AGENT still drives the finder's agentic dispatch, but the front-matter now contradicts the routing tier and is a latent trap for anyone reasoning about tooling from the prompt alone

findings.finding: The plan's load-bearing mechanism half (approach step 3: an LLM criterion `project.measurement-provenance` that reads infra/ and turns the wrong-account escape into a repo-checkable contradiction) cannot load as specified, because Scope omits the required project-criterion rubric prompt and never pins the criterion's exec tier. Every activated non-DET project.* criterion resolves its rubric body from `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-<name>.md`; without `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md` the criterion raises PromptNotFound, and unless it is exec: AGENT it gets no filesystem tooling to read `infra/terraform/versions.tf` at all.
findings.location: Approach step 3 + Scope 'In scope' list; AC lines 2/3/8 (contradiction / contrast / no-anchor tests)
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope 'In scope', add the rubric prompt file `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md` (authored like the existing project.* rubrics), and specify the `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` entry as `exec: "AGENT"` (mirroring project.symbol-reference-completeness) so the criterion receives filesystem tooling to read the IaC backend.

findings.finding: The plan defines a new LLM-tier criterion project.measurement-provenance (Approach step 3, 'Let an LLM criterion judge the declaration against repo facts') but never names or specifies its reviewer rubric prompt file. In this codebase an activated LLM-tier project criterion resolves its rubric from .rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-<name>.md (registry.build_descriptor -> get_prompt(criterion_prompt_id(...)); the routing entry's 'checklist' is empty for every project criterion). The criterion's decision rules — the declared-vs-repo anchor-matching, the no-anchor fallback, and the privilege_posture judgement — are described only in Testing/ACs and are never co-located with a defined rubric the executor is instructed to author; without that prompt the descriptor cannot be built and the whole LLM half of the mechanism cannot run.
findings.location: ## Scope > In scope (artifact list) and ## Approach step 3
findings.suggested_fix: Add '.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md — the LLM reviewer rubric (finding threshold, required fields, privilege_posture enum, declared-environment-vs-repo-IaC anchor/contradiction rule, no-anchor fallback), modeled on .rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md' to the In-scope list, and an AC: 'the criterion is loadable — its rubric exists at .rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md and a test resolves the descriptor via the registry.'
